title: A `bool` route capture is never converted: it matches any segment and arrives as text.
text: `#[Core\Route(path: "/u/{b}", …)] public function a(bool $b)` passes `nvs check`, since `rule:security/route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type` and the capture type list admit `bool`. The crossing maps `bool` to `CaptureConv::Unconverted` (`capture_conv` in `crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs`), so `/u/yes`, `/u/0` and `/u/true` all match and `$match->param("b")` is the segment's text (`string(3) "yes"`), not a `bool`. `Core\Router::url("u", ["b" => false])` builds `/u/`, a link the route does not match. Whether `Core\Router::dispatch` then hands a string to the `bool` parameter was not probed; `capture_value` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/router.rs` binds a `Param::Text` as a string whatever the parameter's type. `E0752`'s help lists the types a capture or a `#[Query]` takes and leaves out `bool` (`crates/nvs-types/src/routes.rs`), so the help and the checker disagree too. It closes when a `bool` capture converts (or is refused with `E0752`), with a conformance case for the match, the link and the dispatch.
